name: Myrddin

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Myrddin is a Welsh hero. His story gave the world the magician Merlin. The British writer Geoffrey of Monmouth called him Wild Merlin. In the tale Myrddin was a king who went mad. He fled to the woods like the Irish king Suibhne. The madness came from the horror of battle. The fight at Arfderydd broke his mind. He ran to Scotland to heal. There he found his power of prophecy. The Celts linked madness with war. The Irish war goddess Nemain carried frenzy. Myrddin then stood as a prophet, mad and wise together, awaiting an age when the quiet would return.
